subject: Residency & hosting tradeoffs — EU-first requirement and APAC fallback
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Holm <sophie.holm@clearpath.fi>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick recap + residency question from today's demo

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. I wanted to capture the key points and one outstanding item that affects the hosting recommendation.

Summary from call:
- Primary requirement: all customer data and inference for consumer-facing features must remain in EU jurisdictions (Finland + EU data centers).
- Secondary: a small set of partner integrations (billing, analytics) run in APAC; those calls currently leave Finland and hit our partner endpoints in Tokyo.
- Traffic profile: 95% EU low-latency requests, ~5% bursts from partners coming from APAC.

Key question for qualification:
Do you require strict in-country (Finland-only) residency, or is EU-only (data stored and processed within EU regions) acceptable? That will drive whether we recommend Hosted API with EU-only routing, Redwood Dedicated (reserved EU capacity), or a Private VPC (customer-managed, EU-only).

Proposed next steps:
1) If EU-only is acceptable, we'll propose a Hosted setup with regional routing + optional Dedicated pool for SLA-critical paths.
2) If Finland-only required, we'll put together a Private VPC proposal and estimate on-prem / colocation options.
3) I'll loop in our solutions lead (Marissa) to outline the dataflow impact and a short matrix of tradeoffs.

Attachment: I dropped an initial data flow stub in case helpful (data_flow_diagram.png).

Could you confirm residency granularity (Finland-only vs EU-wide) and call out if any partners must be allowed to reach inference endpoints from APAC?

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Sophie Holm <sophie.holm@clearpath.fi>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Akira Tanaka <akira.tanaka@tokyo-bank.jp>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Quick recap + residency question from today's demo

Hi Connor — thanks for the summary. Short answers below.

- Residency: EU-only is acceptable for most inference processing. We do not have a strict Finland-only legal requirement today, but our compliance team prefers keeping primary data within EU regions.
- APAC partners: Akira (cc'd) runs an external billing partner in Tokyo that will occasionally call our APIs for verification. We would like requests from that partner to be allowed, but prefer routing/ingress controls so tokens/data don't get stored outside EU.
- SLA: for customer-facing flows we need 99.9% uptime and <120ms median inference latency for common 1k token prompts.

Can you outline how Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private would handle the APAC partner traffic without violating residency?

Best,
Sophie Holm
Product Manager | ClearPath Financial
Sophie.Holm@clearpath.fi

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Holm <sophie.holm@clearpath.fi>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Akira Tanaka <akira.tanaka@tokyo-bank.jp>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + residency question from today's demo

Thanks Sophie — helpful. Looping in Marissa (Solutions) and Ben (Technical AE) to propose concrete options. Below are the tradeoffs at a high-level so we can be actionable in a follow-up.

High-level options (EU-residency-first):

1) Hosted API (EU regions only)
- How it works: Redwood serves inference from our EU-hosted fleet; storage and inference are pinned to EU regions.
- APAC partner traffic: we can accept partner requests but configure an ingress proxy to route their calls through our EU edge, terminate, and process in EU (so data never persists in APAC). Additional authentication and allowlist rules applied.
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra to manage; supports regional failover.
- Cons: shared tenancy; for very strict customers, Dedicated or Private is preferred.

2) Dedicated (reserved EU capacity)
- How it works: Dedicated GPU pools located in EU region(s) for your account only; predictable throughput and SLA.
- APAC partner traffic: same proxy pattern as Hosted; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and guaranteed performance.
- Pros: SLA-backed, capacity committed, stronger data isolation within our infra.
- Cons: commit cost; may need capacity planning for burst windows.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
- How it works: Customer-managed VPC in EU region(s) or on-prem colocation with Redwood runtime; full network control and data never leaves customer-managed network unless configured.
- APAC partner traffic: you can choose to expose a controlled ingress bridge (e.g., API gateway in EU) so partner calls are terminated in EU; no cross-border data egress unless explicitly configured.
- Pros: maximum control and compliance; ideal for regulated use cases.
- Cons: longer setup, operational overhead.

Action items I propose:
- Marissa: can you draft a 1-pager matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with estimated cost buckets and a recommended baseline for ClearPath's traffic profile? Please include the proxy pattern and any additional controls (KMS, audit logs, ingress allowlist).
- Connor: I'll schedule a short 30-min follow-up next week to review the matrix and confirm appetite for a Dedicated POC vs Hosted launch.
- Sophie / Akira: if you agree, share any written compliance constraints from legal or your security team (short bullet list).

Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Holm <sophie.holm@clearpath.fi>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + residency question from today's demo

Hi Sophie — added technical clarifications and a recommended baseline. See attached (redwood_hosting_matrix.xlsx) for a compact comparison. Below are the things I think matter most for your decision.

Technical clarifications:
- Ingress proxy design: we recommend an EU-edge proxy (TLS terminate in EU) that performs request validation and strips any PII before passing to the inference runtime. This ensures partner-originated traffic never writes to non-EU storage.
- KV / cache behavior: if you use prefix caching for performance, we will scope caches to EU-only clusters. Cross-region cache replication is off by default; we only enable it when explicitly requested.
- Metrics & audits: Dedicated and Private both provide per-token audit logs with retention policy controls; Hosted can also provide logs but they are aggregated unless you opt for longer retention.

Recommended baseline for ClearPath (based on 95% EU, 5% APAC partner):
- Launch: EU-hosted with EU-only routing + ingress proxy, short Dedicated commit for peak windows (monthly) to cover SLA-sensitive flows.
- If Legal requires absolute data separation later: plan Private VPC transition; we can design migration so model endpoints and keys rotate during the cutover.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Sophie: send any compliance bullets (expected by Tue 17 Nov).
2) Marissa: I will send the hosting matrix and a 2-week Dedicated trial estimate (attached).
3) Connor: schedule 30-min follow-up for Wed 18 Nov 08:30 CET — include Akira if possible.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_hosting_matrix.xlsx
